contexts.title: Paper 1, Section C, Question 1
contexts.markdown:
Consider a function f which, for integer input x, returns the remainder of (ax² + bx + c) divided by 3. a, b, c are equal to 0, 1, or 2. We denote this return value by f(x).

Here is an example. Suppose a = 0, b = 2, c = 0. Then, when the input x is −1, f(x) equals 1, because:

ax² + bx + c = 0 · (−1)² + 2 · (−1) + 0 = −2,

and the remainder of −2 divided by 3 is 1.

The values of a, b, and c are unknown to you, and you want to find them out by making queries. Each time you make a query, you can pick an integer x as input, and you will then receive the value of f(x).

In the following questions, you need to determine the minimum number of queries needed to find out the value of one unknown (a, b, or c). Note that you do not need to find out the values of the other two. If it is impossible to do so, write X as your answer.

contexts.title: Paper 1, Section C, Question 2
contexts.markdown:
Alice and Peter are playing a game of numbers! Rules of the game are as follows:

In the beginning of the game, each of Alice and Peter has an array of n integers. Alice and Peter take turns to remove an element from their array, with Alice being the first to move. The game ends when there is one element remaining in each of Alice’s and Peter’s array.

Alice tries to maximise the absolute difference of the 2 remaining elements, while Peter tries to minimise it. Suppose Alice and Peter both play optimally, find the absolute difference of the remaining elements.

contexts.title: Paper 2 (Python), Section C, Question 1
contexts.markdown:
A binary sequence a is a list of n integers a[0], a[1], · · · , a[n - 1] where all entries are either 0 or 1.

Given a binary sequence a, a trough is a triplet of indices (i, j, k), such that 0 ≤ i < j < k < n and a[i] = 1, a[j] = 0, a[k] = 1. For example, if the binary sequence is 001101, then its troughs are (2, 4, 5) and (3, 4, 5).

prompt.en:
Let a be a list of integers of length n, where n ≥ 1. A left circular shift on the list is defined as setting a[0], a[1], · · · , a[n-3], a[n-2], a[n-1] to be a[1], a[2], · · · , a[n-2], a[n-1], a[0] simultaneously.

For example, if n = 5 and a = [1,2,3,4,5]. a would become [2,3,4,5,1] after one left circular shift.

Complete the following function left_shift(a) that performs left circular shift on list a once.
